name: SimpleX Chat
insteadOf: WhatsApp / Telegram / Signal (all built on your phone number)
hook: The first messenger with no user identifiers at all — no phone number, no email, no username — just private chats you accept by invitation.
bullets: No user IDs: you are never addressable without first sending an invitation link
End-to-end encrypted by default for messages, files, images, and calls
Decentralized — chat over servers you can run yourself, which store no metadata
Groups, voice and video calls, multi-device profiles, and huge file transfers
benefits: Nobody can enumerate, scrape, or spam you — contact only happens by your invitation
Metadata-private: servers cannot see who talks to whom, only encrypted payloads
Your identity is whatever link you share — rotate it and start fresh
Works in censored networks and over Tor without special configuration
setupSteps: Install SimpleX from F-Droid, the website, or GitHub releases
Create a local profile — no phone number or email is ever requested
Share your one-time invitation link or QR code with people you want to reach
Optionally point the app at your own SMP server for full self-hosting
details: SimpleX Chat is a messenger built on a genuinely different premise: instead of assigning users identifiers — phone numbers, emails, even random handles — it connects people through one-time invitation links and rotating private keys, so there is nothing on any server to enumerate or breach. Messages, files, and calls are end-to-end encrypted with the Double Ratchet algorithm, and the network itself is decentralized: the SMP servers that relay messages can be self-hosted, hold no user accounts, and are designed so they cannot even tell who is talking to whom. On top of that sit the conveniences you expect — group chats, voice and video calls, multiple devices per profile, message forwarding across servers for censorship resistance, and multi-gigabyte file transfers. It is AGPL-3.0, audited, and available on F-Droid; the trade-off is a slightly different mental model, since every conversation starts from an invitation link rather than a contact list.
setup: App (Android) — create a profile, share an invitation link
